title: No-Reserve 1994 Acura Integra GS-R With Vertical Doors Was an Extra in '2 Fast 2 Furious' - Motorious
content: Classic car news, hand-picked vehicles, and auction coverage. Choose what lands in your inbox. Few cars wear the early-2000s tuner look as completely as this one. A 1994 Acura Integra GS-R hatchback on Bring a Trailer is listed with vertically opening doors, a Jackson Racing supercharger and a claim to 2 Fast 2 Furious screen time. It is being offered at no reserve, with bidding at $1,320 as of this writing and the auction ending Monday, November 30. According to the listing, the owner's late father bought the Integra in 1996 and the car was later used as an extra in 2 Fast 2 Furious. The seller says RavenWood Paint and Body applied the custom black-and-red paint in 2003 following filming. In the auction comments, the seller said he is helping sell the car for a family that lost its father. That film-era connection puts it in the same orbit as other cars from the franchise we have covered, including Paul Walker's 2 Fast 2 Furious Evo and the Petersen Museum's Fast & Furious anniversary exhibit. Unlike those, this one is a background player, and there is no film documentation described in the listing beyond the seller's account. Under the hood is the 1.8-liter DOHC VTEC four-cylinder, fitted with a Jackson Racing supercharger, an aftermarket intake and Comptech dress-up parts, plus a Comptech strut tower brace. Power goes to the front wheels through a five-speed manual transaxle. The listing does not state a horsepower figure. Underneath, the Integra rides on 19-inch HRE ten-spoke wheels wrapped in 255/40 Firestone Firehawk tires, with drilled and slotted rotors and SSBC Force 10 front calipers behind them. It is the kind of build that fans of the car's tuning culture will recognize from our look at the world's fastest Integra, though this one leans toward show-and-shine rather than record runs. The headline modification is the set of vertically opening doors, joined by a body kit, aftermarket headlights, a rear wing and a power sunroof. Inside, the black-and-red upholstery gets a Momo steering wheel and pedal covers, carbon-look trim, a Sony head unit and a Clarion screen. The cargo area holds Sony Xplod subwoofers, an amplifier and a CD changer, while auxiliary gauges sit on the driver's A-pillar and an A'PEXi V-AFC controller rides on the dashboard. The odometer shows about 72,000 miles. The listing says the car comes with the owner's manual, service records and an Arizona title, and the CARFAX report shows no accidents or damage. The seller notes that the air conditioning was serviced in October 2026 and that the turn signals do not self-cancel. The car is located in Peoria, Arizona. CARFAX lists a single owner, and the car has been offered by a private party. If you want more Integra reading while the bidding runs, our story on the Integra Type R that took on a G80 M3 shows the nameplate in a very different, modern light. When European procurement managers evaluate cleaning appliances for retail shelves, expectations have shifted away from superficial aesthetic appeal toward rigorous safety verification. In home cleaning and textile maintenance sectors, electrical safety, temperature rise control, and mechanical protection have become strict baseline metrics. Buyers no longer select products based solely on suction power numbers; instead, they examine how internal components withstand continuous operational stress. Within this shifting trade environment, Yiwu Saiwei Household Appliances Co., Ltd. (Amare) has established a robust operational foothold by aligning manufacturing precision with international safety expectations. As a specialized enterprise focusing on textile maintenance devices, Amare operates as a China leading carpet spot cleaning machine supplier, addressing the rigorous demands of global distribution networks through systematic quality control. The contemporary supply chain environment places considerable emphasis on verifiable reliability at the factory level. Retailers across Western Europe and North America scrutinize supplier credentials down to individual component tolerances and circuit board layouts. When sourcing a carpet spot cleaning machine, procurement teams look for manufacturers who can demonstrate consistent output without compromising on electrical insulation or thermal management. This operational reality requires production facilities to maintain tight tolerances during plastic injection molding, motor assembly, and wiring harness installation. By integrating advanced testing instruments directly into production lines, manufacturing plants can filter out potential defects before final packaging. The Significance of GS Certification in European Markets Quality assurance frameworks in export destinations rely heavily on recognized third-party safety marks. The GS mark, standing for Geprüfte Sicherheit, represents an authoritative German safety certification recognized throughout the European Union. Tested strictly against European Norm standards by accredited independent testing institutions, this mark verifies that a product meets statutory safety requirements regarding mechanical strength, electrical insulation, ergonomic design, and chemical composition. Although the GS mark is technically voluntary under European product legislation, major German retailers, DIY warehouse chains, and regional distributors treat it as a mandatory prerequisite for market entry. Compared to the CE marking, which relies primarily on manufacturer self-declaration, the GS mark requires factory inspections and independent laboratory testing of physical samples. This distinction makes GS certification a formidable benchmark for overseas suppliers seeking entry into premium retail channels. Retail buyers recognize that products bearing this safety mark have undergone rigorous evaluation regarding potential hazards such as short circuits, overheating, user burns, and toxic material emissions. Consequently, achieving GS compliance transforms a standard household appliance into a trusted consumer commodity. Manufacturers who invest in this certification demonstrate a long-term commitment to consumer protection and regulatory transparency, distinguishing their offerings in crowded retail environments. Meeting stringent German safety standards requires meticulous attention to engineering and internal component design. At its manufacturing facility in Zhejiang, Yiwu Saiwei Household Appliances Co., Ltd. implements dedicated engineering protocols to ensure that every device meets mechanical and electrical safety requirements. The company's core product lineup includes versatile 500W spot cleaning units engineered for deep textile extraction. These compact machines utilize proprietary self-developed water pumps and heating elements designed to balance cleaning efficiency with thermal stability during extended operation cycles. To prevent fluid ingress into sensitive electrical compartments, these 500W units feature a deliberate clean and wastewater separation architecture. The dual-tank configuration isolates fresh cleaning solution from extracted wastewater, preventing cross-contamination and reducing the risk of internal short circuits. Furthermore, integrated overflow prevention sensors automatically halt water intake when recovery tanks reach maximum capacity. Motor overheating protection mechanisms monitor operational temperatures in real time, cutting power supply automatically if thermal thresholds are exceeded due to restricted airflow or extended continuous use. Beyond internal fluid dynamics, the structural integrity of the appliance plays a critical role in mechanical safety. Precision metal and plastic molds ensure that housing components maintain exact wall thicknesses and tight assembly clearances. This dimensional consistency eliminates loose panel gaps where moisture or dust could penetrate internal circuitry. Strain reliefs on power cords and secure internal wiring harnesses prevent wire fraying or disconnection under mechanical vibration. By combining robust thermal management, precise fluid isolation, and durable mechanical housing, Amare ensures that its carpet spot cleaning machine achieves the structural reliability necessary to pass rigorous GS laboratory evaluations. A credible safety certification is only as reliable as the manufacturing consistency behind it. To maintain continuous compliance with European standards, export suppliers must implement comprehensive batch tracking and quality traceability systems. In modern factory operations, accountability extends from raw material intake to final packaging and palletization. Each manufactured unit receives a unique laser-etched serial number and production batch barcode, linking the finished appliance to specific material lots, component suppliers, and assembly shift logs. When independent auditors inspect production facilities for GS surveillance audits, they examine these traceability records to verify that mass-produced items match the exact specifications of the original tested prototype. Critical components such as thermostats, power switches, pump motors, and internal wiring cables are sourced from qualified tier-one suppliers with verifiable material test reports. Yiwu Saiwei Household Appliances Co., Ltd. archives all incoming material inspection certificates and end-of-line electrical safety test logs in a centralized digital database. This rigorous documentation process enables channel distributors and retail buyers to trace safety data instantly if quality inquiries arise. If a specific batch requires verification, quality assurance personnel can retrieve electrical insulation test results, high-voltage breakdown test records, and functional test logs within minutes. This level of operational transparency reassures commercial partners that product safety is managed through systematic engineering protocols rather than random spot checks. Such structured traceability reinforces long-term trust between Chinese manufacturing enterprises and international trade partners. title: How Hedge Funds Are Navigating Stock Market Volatility - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Analysis and forecasts on global economies and markets for the year ahead from economists and strategists across Goldman Sachs. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. Hedge funds are reducing risk and hedging their portfolios with short positions amid volatility in technology stocks, says Vincent Lin, co-head of Prime Insights and Analytics in Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities. While “faster money” types, including hedge funds using momentum strategies, are being more cautious, "slower money" investment among retirement savers remains historically elevated. In The Markets podcast, Lin also highlights opportunities in hyperscalers and in defensive sectors like healthcare. Chris Hussey: This is The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey, and today is Monday, November 23rd, and I'm here on the Goldman Sachs trading floor with Vincent Lin, who is co-head of Prime Insights and Analytics within our FICC and Equities business. And today we're going to talk a lot about the hedge fund volatility, market volatility that's taking place, how hedge fund customers are holding up in this environment, and what's the path for the year ahead. Chris Hussey: Okay, Vinny, let's start with the volatile market that we've had because last week, big sell-off. This week, bouncing back a little bit. Amidst it all, a big spike in vol. What do you make of it? And more importantly, what are our hedge fund clients telling you is happening? Vincent Lin: If we take a step back, right, the performance backdrop within the overall hedge fund complex has become a lot more challenging the past few months. This was particularly true for the month of October, and I would say November month to date as well, coming into today. So, we have seen our hedge fund clients unwinding risk, so essentially degrossing activity for five straight weeks before last week. So, collectively, hedge fund clients have been paring back a lot of their net exposures and also gross exposures recently as well. I think what's changed last week is that even though the overall degrossing activity stopped, we actually have seen hedge fund clients become incrementally more cautious by adding shorts, right? So, they were in the market adding a lot of short positions across both single stocks and also macro products, meaning index futures and ETFs, so essentially the market hedges. For context, last week our hedge fund clients added ETF shorts by about 19 percentage points just in the past week, which would be the third-largest weekly increase we have seen in the past decade. So clearly, I think there's a lot of uncertainty and also fragile sentiment being expressed by our hedge fund clients. Chris Hussey: Yeah, very fragile sentiment. Obviously, that can be expressed with shorts. That can also be expressed with longs, though. What are they rotating into? What are you seeing our hedge fund clients rotating into? Vincent Lin: Yeah. So, if we look at the overall market on a sector industry level, right, sectors like consumer staples, utilities, and also REITs. Kind of the defensive sectors have meaningfully outperformed the market in the past month. Coincidentally, those are also the sectors that hedge fund clients have sold a lot less, right, versus say tech or the AI infrastructure space in the past month. And I think the reason being that obviously, those are defensive sectors carrying a lot lower beta versus the overall market, but they are also the sectors that are much less exposed to overall consumer spending, for example, as well as having low correlations to AI. Chris Hussey: Vinny, a lot of those defensive trades are also rate-sensitive trades. How much of this is a bet on rates? Vincent Lin: So, within the tech complex, we have seen our hedge fund clients gravitate toward the hyperscalers, which is obviously much higher quality in terms of balance sheet, in terms of their defensive characteristics with regards to earnings. And then secondly, on the short side, right? Our hedge fund clients actually have been actively shorting some of the more recessive pockets within the consumer space. For example, housing, including home builders. That's where I think positioning has been declining to pretty much multi-year lows on the PB book, and that's primarily driven by short additions. Chris Hussey: All right, let's back away from your hedge fund expertise, and I want to ask you about the retail investor, the individual investors out there, because over the course of 2026, we've seen that individual investor get very long and then pull back from the market and then get long again. Going into this, you got a sense that the individual investor was long again. How much of this volatility that we're seeing is being caused not by our hedge fund community, but individuals? Vincent Lin: If I can break up the positioning in terms of two cohorts, right? I would say fast money versus slow money. If I look at the fast money types, meaning hedge funds or CTAs, meaning momentum-driven strategies, their positionings are pretty close to either multi-year lows or toward the bottom end of the historical range. I'll argue some of the faster money retail kind of day trader types, we certainly have seen, you know, less enthusiastic trading activity in some of the more retail-driven pockets of the market in the past month. However, if I look at the slower money, meaning kind of the household 401K mutual funds type of accounts, a case can be made that their positioning is still fairly elevated versus history. In fact, if I look at, the overall ETF and mutual fund complex, collectively they have attracted $150 billion of inflows in the past month, and this is happening in the middle of the market drawdown. Chris Hussey: Yeah, no, very interesting. The households still own a lot of stocks. All right. Let me ask you about, a little bit about the Santa Rally, because you mentioned earlier that the hedge fund community was sort of going into this sell-off with poor performance overall. Does that set us up for a rally, or do you feel that they're going to fade any rally here? Vincent Lin: So, I think in historical periods when we see elevated macro uncertainty, particularly coupled with a lack of clarity in earnings outlook going into next year, I think there's a phrase being thrown around meaning buyers live higher, and I think this dynamic applies here, right? Both for the fundamental long short community because of the performance drawdown that we have seen in the past month, I think managers generally speaking, despite positioning already at this price levels, they want to see some more stabilization in market prices. Given the fact that there's not much time left toward the end of the year, I think our hedge fund clients are still more in a capital preservation mode than chasing the tape. And then secondly, if I look at the systematic, the momentum-driven community, our future strats model forecast is also calling for more constructive flows if price can stabilize from here or even trend higher. So, I think buyers live higher is what I would describe it. Chris Hussey: One last quick question around that. Is there anything that your hedge fund clients are seeing from a fundamental standpoint, or that is getting them to want to sell the market here? Either it is credit spreads widening or any element of that. Are you seeing anything? Vincent Lin: I would say and I know we'll touch on performance, but performance drawdown, it has been an issue. And typically, when you are not making money, your risk appetite, in terms of deploying more capital has been reduced. So, that's by far the biggest factor. The second one, I think, you know, from a fundamental perspective, the AI narratives have clearly gotten more challenging. And I think most of the sentiment or conversation we're having is that the best of the AI infrastructure returns is probably behind us. So essentially, the AI trade is starting to transition from, you know, kind of the AI infrastructure layer to the monetization and returns and the use cases of the AI infrastructure trade. And historically, especially, in the middle of this kind of as big of a technology cycle like we're in right now, the transition period is always the most difficult. Chris Hussey: Yeah. And so, let's touch on that performance element of it, because you mentioned it. Are hedge funds now in a good enough performance period where they can add risk, or do you feel like nah? Vincent Lin: Take a step back, look at first half of the performance. Obviously, our equity fundamental long-short clients in midyear, they were up a lot. About 17% on an asset-weighted basis. And like I mentioned, the last few month has been difficult because that cohort is the most exposed to the AI theme. But even after the recent drawdown, they're still up 7% coming into today. Vincent Lin: So down but not out is what we describe it. Also equally important, if I move away from the fundamental long-short cohorts, if I look at the performance of our systematic long-short clients, meaning quant equities, their returns actually have strengthened since midyear. So even though the fundamental long-short cohort have suffered a pretty sharp drawdown, there's still much more dispersion going around. And I think hedge funds collectively are still holding up. And then, I think one last thing I'll mention is we have noted in our past reports that hedge funds, really since COVID, have done much better versus a traditional 60/40 equity bond portfolio, and I think that dynamic is still intact. Chris Hussey: All right, Vinny, lots to digest here. Let's put a bow on it. What's the trade? Vincent Lin: So within the tech and AI complex, I still like the hyperscalers. In the scenario that the compute capacities remains constrained, I think they will be relative winners. Also, if we do see evidence of AI CapEx growth start to decelerate meaningfully from here, the more positive free cash flow dynamic and generation is going to open up a lot more capital deployment possibilities, including share buyback. Within the defensive space, I like healthcare over staples. One, I think valuation is a lot more attractive. Also, secondly, there are multiple secular earnings drivers within the space that are also less exposed to AI. Chris Hussey: All right. Last question for you because we're going to be moving into December next week, and we'll have a whole new set of catalysts. Vincent Lin: So first of all, this week we'll have multiple late cycle tech reporters. I think those are going to be important to watch for kind of the latest spending on AI. And then secondly, I think for the remainder of this year, it's going to be dominated by macroeconomic prints, right? So, later this week we'll have PCE, next week we'll have payroll, and then three weeks from now we'll have the November CPI. I think those collectively are going to be important to gauge in terms of determining the Fed's next move, not only for December, but also going to next year. Is the more recently hawkish posture warranted, or can we see possibly some evidence of a dovish turn? Chris Hussey: Vinny, always a wealth of information. Thanks so much. Chris Hussey: That does it for this week's episode of The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey. Thanks for listening. title: GS Group Promotes Hur Suh-hong to Retail President - 조선일보
content: Promotions include fourth-generation family members, reflecting stability amid external challenges GS Group's regular executive reshuffle promoted Hur Suh-hong (49), CEO and vice president of GS Retail, to president. President Hur, the eldest son of Heo Gwang-su, chairman of Samyang International, and a fifth cousin of Huh Tae-soo, GS Group chairman, was promoted to president approximately two years after becoming CEO. Additionally, Lee Tae-hyung (56), vice president and head of the CFO (Chief Financial Officer) and PM (Portfolio Management) team at GS Corporation, the group’s holding company, was also promoted to president. This year’s reshuffle included a total of 40 people, including two presidents, maintaining a similar scale to previous years. Unlike last year, which saw leadership changes in nine subsidiaries, this year’s reshuffle retained all CEOs of major subsidiaries, reflecting an emphasis on stability amid heightened external instability. Other promotions among the fourth-generation members of the owner family included Huh Chi-hong (43), former head of GS Retail’s Strategy Division, and Huh Joo-hong (43), head of the Basic Chemicals Division at GS Caltex, both elevated to vice president. Huh Joo-hong will oversee the C&L (Chemical & Lubricants) division, which manages petrochemical and lubricant businesses. Huh Chi-hong is the son of Huh Jin-soo, advisor to GS Caltex, while Huh Joo-hong is the son of Heo Myung-su, senior advisor to GS Engineering & Construction.

title: FIRST RIDE | BMW F450 GS makes adventure riding more accessible - TimesLIVE
content: BMW Motorrad has launched the new F450 GS as its entry-level adventure motorcycle in South Africa. Replacing the single-cylinder G310 GS, it is a more powerful machine with a twin-cylinder 420cc engine and is BMW’s latest contender in the growing market segment of medium-displacement bikes. Like its larger stablemates in the GS range, it is a versatile all-rounder, combining everyday usability, touring comfort and off-road capability. Its more accessible price and manageable power output should appeal to beginners without disappointing more experienced riders. The bike’s tractable power delivery is one of the things that impressed me most when I rode it at the South African media launch in Gauteng earlier this week. On roads that took us along popular breakfast-run routes in Hartbeespoort, as well as on gravel trails, the engine felt punchier than I expected for its small size. The parallel-twin engine, with outputs of 35kW at 8,750 rpm and 43Nm at 6,750 rpm, proved to have a free-revving nature that gave the medium-sized bike a zesty spring in its step, whether pulling off or overtaking slower traffic. With a top speed of around 170km/h, it has good touring potential too, and the small screen provides decent wind protection at higher speeds. With claimed fuel consumption of 3.8l/100km, the bike has a range of more than 350km on its 14l tank. The engine has a single balance shaft to reduce vibrations and it’s mostly effective, though I felt some buzzy vibrations through the seat at certain revs. The unit has a characteristically fruity twin-cylinder sound without being too noisy. It is packed with much of the technology found in its more expensive stablemates, including standard traction control, engine drag control, heated grips and lean-angle-sensitive anti-lock braking All versions of the bike except the basic version have a quickshifter, which allows clutchless up- and downshifts in the six-speed transmission. Standard on the GS Trophy and optionally available on the other variants is an Easy Ride Clutch (ERC). Using a centrifugal clutch, it allows you to operate the bike without the clutch lever, even when pulling off, but allows the rider to intervene manually at any time if necessary. The F450 GS is a mid-sized bike that won’t feel too intimidating to novice riders. Weighing 178kg, it is a lot smaller and wieldier than the big daddy R1300 GS, which tips the scales at a portly 238kg, but retains the typical GS sense of heft and solid feel, with high-quality finishes. Available in three saddle heights to accommodate various-sized riders, the 450 is also unmistakably a GS in design, with its distinctive flyline, tough-guy looks, tubular steel frame and features such as an LED headlight with an “X” daytime riding light. It is also packed with much of the technology found in its more expensive stablemates, including standard traction control, engine drag control, heated grips and lean-angle-sensitive anti-lock braking. All models have three riding modes — Rain, Road and Enduro — with an additional Enduro Pro mode from the Exclusive model upwards. The latter disables the ABS assistance on the rear wheel, allowing the rider to lock the wheel deliberately when necessary on gravel, giving greater control over braking. On off-road sections of the route, the F450 GS excelled with its comfortable ride and reassuring agility. I was particularly impressed with how yielding the suspension was and how effectively it absorbed bumpy, rippled surfaces. There was no chance to test it in soft sand, but on rough gravel the middleweight BMW displayed the classic GS turf-taming ability. Wider enduro footrests are included from the Exclusive version upwards or are available as optional accessories. The front wheel is guided via KYB upside-down telescopic forks, while the rear wheel has a double-arm swingarm with a KYB central spring strut featuring progressive damping. The Sport and GS Trophy variants feature sports suspension that allows the rider to adjust both rebound and compression damping. All but the base model have handguards and wide off-road footrests, while the range-topping GS Trophy has an aluminium engine guard. The brakes comprise a single 310mm front disc with a Brembo four-piston fixed caliper and a single 240mm rear disc. The F450 GS comes standard with aluminium alloy wheels (19-inch front and 17-inch rear), but is optionally available with more trail-focused spoked wheels. The dual-purpose Maxxis tubeless tyres provided good grip both on and off the tar. The 6.5-inch TFT display is legible in sunlight and menus are accessed via an iDrive-style rotary controller. There is a USB-C socket, and taking phone calls, listening to music and using navigation while riding are all possible via smartphone and helmet pairing. title: Vikran Engineering faces ₹12.50 crore claim in litigation with GS Products India - Business Upturn
content: Vikran Engineering Limited has disclosed a significant legal development concerning a claim raised by M/s. GS Products India amounting to ₹12.50 crore. The company made this announcement in compliance with Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, following an administrative warning from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) dated 4th November 2026. The litigation involves a claim that was presented by GS Products India to the MSME Facilitation Council in October 2025. As of now, Vikran Engineering has responded to the claim, but no further communication regarding subsequent proceedings has been received by the company. This latest disclosure from Vikran Engineering was necessitated by SEBI's advice aiming for enhanced governance, transparency, and investor awareness. The company's board of directors discussed the matter in their meeting on 5th November 2026, where they acknowledged SEBI's communication and pledged to ensure continued transparency in their operations. Despite the substantial claim, Vikran Engineering Limited's current assessment indicates an anticipated additional financial liability of approximately ₹1.81 crore if an adverse order is passed by the competent authority. This estimate was initially assessed as falling below the materiality threshold of ₹3.26 crore as of 31st March 2025, thus impacting the immediacy and nature of prior disclosures. The company emphasised that this disclosure is part of its continued commitment to transparency, ensuring stakeholders are informed about the current situation and its potential financial implications. More details of the litigation, including particulars of the dispute, expected financial implications, and quantum of claims, were attached in an annexure to the formal announcement. The ongoing matter remains a point of concern for Vikran Engineering Limited as they await any further action or communication from the MSME Facilitation Council. The company continues to monitor the situation closely, reiterating its commitment to keeping all relevant parties informed as more information becomes available. title: Goldman Sachs stock: GS Finance files Nasdaq-100 linked notes - ad-hoc-news.de
content: On Tuesday, November 24, 2026, GS Finance Corp. filed a preliminary pricing supplement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for leveraged notes linked to the Nasdaq-100 Futures Excess Return Index. The notes would be guaranteed by The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc., according to the SEC filing. The filing describes securities issued by GS Finance Corp. under its Medium-Term Notes, Series F program. The proposed notes would not pay interest. Their cash settlement would depend on the performance of the Nasdaq-100 Futures Excess Return Index between an expected trade date of December 22, 2026, and an expected determination date of December 22, 2031. The preliminary terms set an upside participation rate of at least 185 percent and a downside buffer at 70 percent of the initial index level. If the index rises, the notes would provide leveraged participation. If the index falls by more than 30 percent, investors could lose part or all of their principal. The final participation rate, issue size and other commercial terms are expected to be set on the trade date. The filing gives an expected original issue date of December 28, 2026, and an expected maturity date of December 26, 2031, subject to the conditions described in the supplement. The document also says that the estimated value at pricing is expected to be below the original issue price, reflecting factors including distribution costs, hedging and credit spreads. The proposed structure gives investors exposure to a futures-based index rather than direct ownership of the companies in the Nasdaq-100. The filing highlights futures-roll effects, market volatility, interest rates and the credit risk of GS Finance Corp. and Goldman Sachs as guarantor. The notes are unsecured obligations and are not bank deposits. Goldman Sachs stock traded at 722.80 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 13:35 CET on Wednesday, November 25. The quote was recorded while the U.S. equity market was open, but the filing itself does not establish a cause for the share price. title: Karol G’s ‘BbY WOW’ spends a seventh week at No. 1 as Christmas songs return - Music Times
content:
Karol G is back at the top of the world chart, and the first Christmas singles of the season have already joined her in the top five. "BbY WOW," by Karol G, Judeline and Rusowsky, rebounded for a seventh week at No. 1 on the Billboard Global 200 and continued for an eighth week atop Billboard Global Excl. U.S., Billboard reported Monday. The song earned 36.5 million streams globally in the Nov. 13-19 tracking week, according to Luminate figures published by Billboard, including 29.8 million streams outside the United States. It first reached No. 1 on both charts in mid-September. The latest charts are dated Nov. 28, 2026, and Billboard said they would update on Billboard.com on Nov. 24. The story, then, is a Monday preview of a chart week that becomes public in full on Tuesday, not a last-minute flash ranking. Beneath Karol G, the Global 200 is a mix of current pop and returning holiday standards. Ashe's "Stop the Wedding!" rises 3-2 for a new Global 200 high, Billboard reported, and Tate McRae's "Housewife" slides two spots to No. 3 after spending its first four weeks at No. 1.
Wham!'s "Last Christmas" climbs 8-4, with 28.8 million streams worldwide, and Mariah Carey's "All I Want for Christmas Is You" climbs 14-5, with 26 million, Billboard said. "Last Christmas" reached No. 1 on the Global 200 for the first time last year, for two weeks. Carey's 1994 standard has now led the chart for 20 weeks, the most since the list began in 2020. The same holiday titles are moving even more sharply on Global Excl. U.S. "Last Christmas" surges 17-5, with 18.5 million streams outside the United States, and "All I Want for Christmas Is You" jumps 35-8, with 16 million. Billboard noted that Wham!'s song spent its first two weeks at No. 1 on Global Excl. U.S. last holiday season, while Carey's has led that chart for 14 weeks. On the same list, "Stop the Wedding!" also lifts 3-2 for a new high, "Housewife" drops 2-3 after three weeks at No. 1, and Jamie Miller's "Babydoll" moves 5-4 for a new peak, Billboard reported. The Billboard Global 200 and Global Excl. U.S. rank songs on streaming and sales activity from more than 200 territories, compiled by Luminate, Billboard said. The Global 200 includes worldwide data. Global Excl. U.S. removes the United States and often tells a clearer story about a song's life outside American radio and streaming. The rankings use a weighted formula of official streams on subscription and ad-supported audio and video services, plus download sales from full-service digital retailers. Sales from direct-to-consumer sites are excluded. The top 100 of each tally is available to all readers on Billboard.com; the complete 200-title lists are behind Billboard Pro. For Karol G, the seventh week at No. 1 is a reminder of how sticky "BbY WOW" has been since mid-September. A rebound, rather than a first-week coronation, means the song lost the top and then took it back as the holiday titles started their annual climb. The Christmas records are doing what they now do every November: entering the top five before Thanksgiving and putting 1980s and 1990s catalog next to current pop. The next public update, according to Billboard, is Tuesday on Billboard.com, for the charts dated Nov. 28. Until then, the picture from the tracking week is already clear. Karol G is No. 1 again, Ashe has a new peak, and Wham! and Mariah Carey are back in the top five.
Billboard also noted that Luminate reviews and authenticates the data used in the weekly rankings, and that submissions deemed suspicious or unverifiable can be removed before the charts are finalized. That process sits behind the 36.5 million global streams figure, but it does not change the published order: Karol G is first, Ashe is second, and the Christmas catalog has arrived early again. A seventh week at No. 1, spread across a run that began in mid-September, is a different achievement from a one-week spike. "BbY WOW" has now lasted long enough to meet the holiday titles on the way back up, which is how a late-November Global 200 often looks: a current international hit at the top, and two December standards already inside the top five. Those two charts also explain why a Latin-pop collaboration can lead the world list while holiday English-language catalog surges underneath it. The Global 200 includes U.S. activity; Global Excl. U.S. does not. "BbY WOW" is even stronger on the latter, where it is in an eighth week at No. 1. The Christmas titles, meanwhile, are climbing both lists at once, which is the seasonal pattern Billboard was documenting, not a one-territory novelty. © 2026 MusicTimes.com All rights reserved. title: NBA Power Rankings: Whom is each team most thankful for this year? - ESPN
content:
As the NBA plays its final games Wednesday night before the Thanksgiving holiday, there is plenty to celebrate around the association as the first full month of the season winds down. MVP front-runners Luka Doncic and Victor Wembanyama have jumped out to sizzling starts, adding to their already impressive résumés as they lead the Los Angeles Lakers and San Antonio Spurs to the top two spots in the West. Meanwhile, Doncic's former Lakers teammate LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers have surged to the top of the East. The Miami Heat are certainly grateful to be the winners of the Giannis Antetokounmpo sweepstakes, riding a seven-game win streak after dropping their first four games of the season. And the Portland Trail Blazers have welcomed Damian Lillard back with open arms, coming off a blowout win over James and the Sixers on Monday night. In this week's Power Rankings, our insiders rank each of the 30 teams and also highlight one player, coach or executive each team should be thankful for as we celebrate Thanksgiving -- with some lamb chops and gravy, of course. POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS Next games: @ POR (Nov. 25), vs. LAL (Nov. 27), vs. BOS (Nov. 29), @ MIL (Nov. 30) In switching to the current guard-heavy starting lineup, San Antonio needed to find ways to optimize the group around franchise superstar Victor Wembanyama. What better way to do that than by bringing in a veteran assistant in Hall of Famer Donovan, who has extensive expertise in that area? Throughout his head coaching tenure in Oklahoma City, Donovan worked with a bevy of dynamic guards such as Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Russell Westbrook, Chris Paul and Dennis Schroder, and understands how to make the spacing work with so many perimeter players on the court together at the same time. The Spurs' new lineup isn't a finished product yet, but the addition of Donovan is helping it round into form quickly. -- Michael C. Wright Next games: @ SA (Nov. 27), @ MEM (Nov. 29), @ HOU (Nov. 30) The 27-year-old supernova is on the short list for the way-too-early MVP contenders (shoutout to our former colleague and current Atlanta Hawks front office member, Tim Bontemps) and has been electric to watch this season, averaging a career-best 36.6 points. It's not only Doncic's scoring that has been a boon for L.A. as it has stayed atop the Western Conference standings. Doncic's sturdy defense -- more recently as a roamer in the Lakers' full-court zone defense and throughout the season with his one-on-one containment (he is second in the NBA in charges drawn) -- caused one team source to tell ESPN that Doncic has been playing "the best defense of his life." -- Dave McMenamin Next games: vs. MIA (Nov. 25), @ IND (Nov. 27), @ HOU (Nov. 28), vs. MEM (Dec. 1) The Sixers play in front of one of the NBA's most passionate fanbases, but also one of its most scorned. It has been 43 years since the Sixers' last title, and for the past decade they endured the infamous tanking era, massive injuries and years of heartbreaking second-round exits. James' signing gave this fanbase real championship hope after years of disappointment. And his impact has been felt early, as the Sixers are off to their best start since 2000-01, which happens to be their most recent finals appearance. -- Kris Rhim Next games: @ OKC (Nov. 25), vs. MEM (Nov. 27), @ SAC (Nov. 29), @ POR (Dec. 1) The Timberwolves didn't officially sign Kuminga until September, months after most of this summer's free agents found new homes. But the long wait has been worth it for both sides: With Minnesota buying time for Anthony Edwards to return from knee surgery, Kuminga has provided valuable contributions on both ends. The athletic forward has averaged 13.4 points and shot 39.7% on 3-pointers in a complementary offensive role, and he's part of a well-balanced starting lineup that has posted an excellent plus-10 net rating without Edwards. -- Ben Golliver Next games: vs. PHX (Nov. 25), vs. PHI (Nov. 28), vs. LAL (Nov. 30), vs. TOR (Dec. 1) Perhaps it's too early to attribute Amen Thompson's shooting improvements to Houston's decision to bring in shooting guru Engelland as an assistant, but you can't discount his track record and reputation around the league, where he's widely regarded as the NBA's best shooting coach. Engelland has worked in the past with Grant Hill, Tony Parker and Kawhi Leonard, along with all of Oklahoma City's young core players, and the results speak for themselves. Thompson should become the latest beneficiary of Engelland's tutelage, along with Reed Sheppard, Jabari Smith Jr. and Tari Eason. -- Wright Next games: vs. CLE (Nov. 25), vs. MIA (Nov. 27), vs. ATL (Nov. 29), @ CHI (Dec. 1) The Knicks look like themselves again, and one big reason has been Towns' consistency. He has had a double-double in every game and leads the NBA in rebounding (13.9). He's playing through the uncertainty of his future as the contract situation hangs over him and the franchise all season long. Still, his shooting splits are ridiculous: 21.8 points on 54/42/76. If there's a reason the Knicks can be counted on to repeat, he's atop the list. -- Vincent Goodwill Next games: @ PHI (Nov. 25), @ NYK (Nov. 27), @ CLE (Nov. 29), vs. ATL (Dec. 1) Despite Giannis Antetokounmpo's MVP-caliber start to the season, we would be remiss to not mention Riley as the person Heat fans should be most thankful for. The list of players Riley has drafted, traded for or signed in Miami is a who's who of current and future Hall of Famers: Alonzo Mourning, Dwyane Wade, Shaquille O'Neal, LeBron James, Chris Bosh, Bam Adebayo, Jimmy Butler and now Antetokounmpo. Miami has won three NBA championships and reached the playoffs in 24 of Riley's 31 seasons with the franchise as head coach and later head of basketball operations. The Antetokounmpo trade has breathed life into a franchise that has not advanced past the first round since the 2022-23 season. -- Bobby Marks Next games: vs. ATL (Nov. 27), @ SA (Nov. 29), @ DAL (Nov. 30) The decision to trade Jaylen Brown for George was so criticized by pundits and Celtics fans alike that even Celtics general manager Brad Stevens acknowledged that fans had a right to be upset about the move. But George has fared well, averaging 19.9 points, 3.8 assists and 5.6 rebounds -- all increases from last season and helping to fuel Boston's top-10 offense. One of his best performances of the season came against his former team, when he scored 36 points in a blowout win earlier this month. -- Rhim Next games: @ UTAH (Nov. 27), @ TOR (Nov. 29), @ DET (Nov. 30) Through 15 games, Murray has been the league's most accurate volume 3-point shooter, making 50 of his 106 attempts. This scorching and efficient scoring from Murray -- 26.2 points on 16.9 shots per game -- has helped the Nuggets sustain a reasonable record (10-5, No. 6 in the West), while many of his teammates are shaking off injury rust and settling into the season. Murray has also received well-deserved plaudits for his improved defensive effort. He is averaging one block and put up this stat line in an overtime win over the Bulls this past weekend: 45 points, seven assists, five rebounds, two blocks, three steals. The Nuggets are plus-96 when he's on the court this season and minus-69 when he's not. -- Anthony Slater Next games: vs. LAC (Nov. 25), @ MIN (Nov. 27), vs. LAL (Nov. 29), @ PHI (Dec. 1) The Memphis general manager slowly dismantled the core of Ja Morant, Jaren Jackson Jr. and Desmond Bane, while embracing a totally new and unconventional style of play to build a different identity with coach Tuomas Isalo. That personnel and philosophical shift took imagination, courage and patience to instill. Grizzlies fans are finally starting to reap the rewards of Kleiman's vision. Memphis signed Ty Jerome in the summer of 2025, and he's averaging a career-high 25.1 points, and selected Cameron Boozer with the third pick of the most recent draft to add to a young core that includes Zach Edey, Cedric Coward and Jaylen Wells. -- Wright Next games: @ BOS (Nov. 27), @ NYK (Nov. 29), @ MIA (Dec. 1) Whom they're thankful for: Nickeil Alexander-Walker Last season's most improved player, Alexander-Walker continues to be one of the best free agents in Hawks history. After averaging a career-high 20.8 PPG last season, Alexander-Walker is averaging 21.3 in two less minutes per game. His $14.4 million salary this season represents one of the better value deals in the league. -- Marks Next games: vs. MIL (Nov. 27), vs. ORL (Nov. 29), vs. DEN (Nov. 30) The Pistons already had Cade Cunningham as their franchise player, along with foundational partners in Jalen Duren and Ausar Thompson, but they endured a record 28-game losing streak in 2023-24. Hiring Bickerstaff to replace Monty Williams one year after Williams had signed a then-record six-year, $78.5 million contract didn't seem as if it would be as fortune-turning as it has been. Bickerstaff has gone 114-66 in two seasons in Detroit, making fans forget how miserable it was before his arrival. The expectations for a deep run into May starts with Bickerstaff's stability on the sidelines, accountability on the court and standards that resonate with the heritage of this franchise -- even staying afloat with the injuries they've suffered this season. -- Goodwill Next games: vs. SA (Nov. 25), vs. GS (Nov. 27), vs. NO (Nov. 29), vs. MIN (Dec. 1) Portland received the ultimate gift when Milwaukee decided to waive and stretch Lillard's contract after his 2025 Achilles tear. Not only did the Blazers get the opportunity to re-sign a franchise icon, but they also snagged Lillard on a bargain contract that pays him $13.4 million in 2026-27 while he remains on Milwaukee's books for $22.5 million every season through 2029-30. Portland is getting All-Star-caliber production from Lillard for its money; Milwaukee is getting absolutely nothing. -- Golliver Next games: vs. MIN (Nov. 25), @ MIL (Nov. 28), @ BKN (Nov. 30) Oklahoma City isn't a franchise that frequently takes big swings in free agency, but general manager Sam Presti strategically targeted Hartenstein in the summer of 2024. Hartenstein proved to be one of the finishing pieces of the Thunder's championship puzzle, providing a physical presence and savvy that Oklahoma City had been missing at center. The veteran, who has averaged a double-double during his Thunder tenure, took a pay cut last summer in signing a three-year, $75 million deal to stay in Oklahoma City. -- Tim MacMahon Fortune favored the Mavs when they won the Flagg sweepstakes, landing the No. 1 pick in the 2025 draft despite only 1.8% odds. Flagg has more than lived up to the hype so far in his NBA career. LeBron James is the only player to record more points, assists and steals than Flagg as a teenager. Months after trading Luka Doncic, Dallas lucked into getting another generational talent to build around. -- MacMahon Next games: @ NYK (Nov. 25), vs. MIA (Nov. 29), vs. IND (Dec. 1) Whom they're thankful for: Tyrese Proctor and Meleek Thomas Cleveland has kept only one of its first-round picks since drafting Evan Mobley in 2021 (that was Jaylon Tyson), but this pair of second-round guards is giving the Cavaliers a much-needed infusion of young talent regardless. Proctor, drafted at No. 49 in 2025, is averaging 9.1 points and making 44% of his 3s. Thomas, drafted with the No. 34 pick in 2026, is averaging 12.7 points and shooting 41% from distance. -- Zach Kram Next games: @ HOU (Nov. 25), vs. DAL (Nov. 27), @ UTAH (Nov. 29), vs. LAC (Dec. 1) There are few things more reliable in the league than Booker putting the ball in the basket for the Suns. The franchise's all-time leading scorer is averaging 24.5 points this season -- his 10th straight season averaging 24 points or more -- and helped his team to eight wins in their past 10 games after starting the season 1-5. The fact that Booker has become a five-time All-Star with the same franchise while playing for enough head coaches to fill a cornucopia (eight different coaches in 12 years), is something Suns fans should not take for granted. -- McMenamin Next games: vs. SAC (Nov. 25), @ POR (Nov. 27), vs. LAC (Nov. 29), vs. UTAH (Dec. 1) Days before training camp, Curry opted to remove any drama about the late stages of his career, signing a two-year extension to deliver the front office an extra $10 million this summer in theoretical cap space and commit to the franchise through his 20th season. "I assumed it would probably be one of, if not the last, contract I signed," Curry told ESPN. "I'm not afraid to say it. But maybe I'll surprise myself and want to keep going." If Curry calls it a career after the 2028-29 season, it will close out two of the greatest individual one-franchise decades in league history. When on the court, he isn't fading quietly. Before his recent oblique injury, Curry was averaging 27.8 points in 26.3 minutes. -- Slater After an injury-filled 2025-26 season, Wagner is putting up All-NBA numbers with the Magic this season. What stands out about Wagner this season is not his scoring (he is on pace to average at least 20 for a third straight season), but that he has nearly tripled his assists per game from 3.3 to 8.3. The Magic are 18 points per 100 possessions better when Wagner is on the court this season. -- Marks After their first two seasons of finishing among the worst teams in the league, the Wizards still didn't have a franchise-altering star to show for all those defeats. In the 2024 draft, they landed the No. 2 pick and drafted Alex Sarr; in the 2025 draft, they fell all the way to No. 6 and landed Tre Johnson. But in a star-driven league like the NBA, one player can make all the difference. The Wizards hope they landed just that player when they won the 2026 lottery and selected Dybantsa at No. 1. -- Kram Next games: vs. BKN (Nov. 27), vs. DEN (Nov. 29), @ HOU (Dec. 1) Though Leonard has played in only two games this season as he manages left knee soreness, his presence in Toronto, paired with All-Star Scottie Barnes, makes this team at full strength a contender in the East. The Raptors haven't made it back to the Finals since Leonard led the team to the title in 2019, and his return, at least on paper, gives them among the best shots to reach a championship again. -- Rhim Next games: vs. PHI (Nov. 27), @ CHI (Nov. 28), @ CLE (Dec. 1) As the team has been ravaged by injuries for a second straight season, Siakam continues to remain Indiana's Mr. Reliable. He has started 17 of the Pacers' 18 games, more than any other member of the starting lineup, and is averaging 22.9 points, 6.2 rebounds and 3.7 assists on 51% shooting. Tyrese Haliburton posted a video to Instagram recently saying he hopes to return from his hamstring injury by the end of November, and he'll be thankful to have Siakam remaining steady by his side when he does. -- Jamal Collier Next games: @ CHA (Nov. 25), vs. IND (Nov. 28), vs. NYK (Dec. 1) After years of middling, miserable seasons, Chicago finally got a payoff last summer by jumping into the top four and landing one of the talented prospects at the top of the draft. Wilson is still a very raw prospect in several respects, but he has arrived in Chicago with confidence, explosiveness and highlight-worthy athleticism, and has given the Bulls their best hope since perhaps the early days of Derrick Rose. Even as Wilson recovers from a broken hand, the Bulls can be thankful for a new face of the franchise. -- Collier Next games: @ MEM (Nov. 25), vs. NO (Nov. 27), @ GS (Nov. 29), @ PHX (Dec. 1) Even in a rebuilding season, Garland has brought stability to the Clippers, averaging the eighth-most points per game (21.3) out of anybody in the top 15 in assists per game (6.6) this season. And at 26, the two-time All-Star is young enough to continue to grow with the team as it hopes to crawl back toward contention. Perhaps the biggest reason Clippers fans should be thankful for Garland's presence is it means 37-year-old James Harden is no longer on the roster. Though Harden is a sure-fire Hall of Famer, and recently turned back the clock with 51 points against the Indiana Pacers, the three-year, $97 million extension he signed with the Cleveland Cavaliers after LA traded him for Garland and a second-round pick is something the Clips would not want on their books going forward. -- McMenamin Next games: vs. CHI (Nov. 25), vs. BKN (Nov. 28), vs. WAS (Nov. 30) Diabate might be the hardest worker in the NBA, as the undersized center is willing himself to a league-leading 5.4 offensive rebounds per game. He originally arrived in Charlotte on a two-way contract in 2024, but he has since transformed into a valuable role player who should enjoy a lengthy career. -- Kram Next games: @ LAC (Nov. 27), @ POR (Nov. 29), @ SAC (Nov. 30) The Pelicans are off to a messy start: They've already suffered seven losses by double digits, and starting guard Dejounte Murray publicly requested a trade after playing only nine games. On the bright side, Williamson has been productive and healthy. The 2019 No. 1 pick has averaged 21.9 points and 5.4 rebounds while posting the best net rating among New Orleans' full-time starters. If New Orleans pursues a much-needed roster shakeup before the trade deadline, Williamson's reliable production could help boost his trade value. -- Golliver Next games: vs. DEN (Nov. 27), vs. PHX (Nov. 29), @ GS (Dec. 1) Utah desperately needed a face-of-the-franchise type of talent when the Jazz finally got some lottery luck, landing the No. 2 pick in this year's draft. The Jazz drafted Peterson because the front office believed he had the highest potential of the players available. Peterson, 19, has flashed glimpses of that potential while averaging 15.9 points and 4.0 assists through the first month-plus of his career. -- MacMahon Next games: @ MIL (Nov. 25), @ TOR (Nov. 27), @ CHA (Nov. 28), vs. OKC (Nov. 30) It would be very easy for Randle to pack it in, to go full malcontent after being traded from one contender to another, then to one of the worst situations in the league in the very town that traded him two years ago (in a deal that subsequently won the Knicks a title). But Randle, for all you can say about him, does care -- hence why he was caught on the bench going off during a blowout loss to the Bulls. And he also wants everyone else to feel it. Because in Brooklyn, somebody has to. -- Goodwill Next games: @ GS (Nov. 25), vs. MIN (Nov. 29), vs. NO (Nov. 30) As another season in Sacramento spirals out of control before December, frustrated Kings fans can take solace in the early returns of their latest lottery pick. Acuff arrived as an unafraid high-volume scorer with advanced playmaking chops. His 22.2 shots per game rank fourth in the NBA. His 24.6 points rank 17th. His 7.2 assists rank 11th. All are tops among rookies. As he develops, Acuff must sharpen his efficiency and improve his defense, and the Kings must build a roster around him that protects his weaknesses. But it has become immediately clear that Sacramento has found a building block. -- Slater Next games: vs. BKN (Nov. 25), @ DET (Nov. 27), vs. OKC (Nov. 28), vs. SA (Nov. 30) The one silver lining for the Bucks during a miserable first month of the season is that their No.10 pick looks like a home run. Burries is averaging 11.4 points, 5.7 rebounds and shooting 45% from the field. He's getting better as the season goes on, finishing with at least double-digit scoring in his past five games, including a career-high 26 points off the bench against Philadelphia last Saturday. title: GS Group elevates fourth-generation founding family member to president as stability anchors reshuffle strategy - Korea JoongAng Daily
content: The conglomerate promoted GS Retail CEO Hur Suh-hong to president while retaining major affiliate chiefs and expanding its next generation of executives. GS Group promoted Hur Suh-hong, a fourth-generation member of its founding family and CEO of GS Retail, to president on Wednesday, while keeping the chief executives of its major affiliates in place. The 2027 reshuffle covers 40 executives: two promotions to president, four new CEOs, six promotions to senior executive vice president, four to senior vice president and 24 newly appointed vice presidents. Unlike last year, when GS replaced the CEOs of nine affiliates, this year's reshuffle prioritized management stability and business continuity. Hur Suh-hong is the eldest son of Samyang International Chairman Hur Kwang-soo, a cousin of GS Group Chairman Huh Tae-soo. Huh and Hur are different spellings of the same Korean surname. Hur Suh-hong worked at GS Energy and GS Holdings before becoming CEO of GS Retail. As head of the future business team at GS Holdings, he led the group's acquisition of botulinum toxin maker Hugel, which helped diversify its businesses. Since taking the helm, Hur Suh-hong has focused on strengthening GS Retail's core businesses and on transforming its operations through AI. GS Retail posted record quarterly consolidated revenue and operating profit in the third quarter this year, helped by record convenience store sales and sharply higher operating profit at its supermarket and home shopping businesses. The recovery in its core businesses and improvements to its business structure are seen as the reasons behind his promotion. Lee Tae-hyoung, the chief financial officer of GS Holdings and head of its portfolio management team, was also promoted to president. Born in 1970, he started out as an engineer at the Yeosu refinery of Honam Oil Refinery, now GS Caltex. He later served as head of corporate planning at GS Energy and CEO of Incheon Total Energy Company, a GS Energy subsidiary. Lee Tae-hyoung was credited with keeping the group's finances sound while supporting its search for new businesses such as AI data centers. He will now coordinate investment priorities and funding plans to back Chairman Huh Tae-soo's growth strategy. Other fourth-generation family members also took on bigger roles. Huh Joo-hong, a GS Caltex executive, and Huh Chi-hong, head of GS Retail's strategy division, were both promoted to senior executive vice president. Huh Joo-hong is the son of Huh Myung-soo, a standing adviser at GS Engineering & Construction (GS E&C), and Huh Chi-hong is the son of GS Caltex adviser Huh Jin-soo. Huh Joo-hong will head GS Caltex's chemicals and lubricants division, which oversees its petrochemical and lubricant businesses. Huh Chi-hong will coordinate GS Retail's companywide strategy and look for growth through overseas business and investment. GS also promoted executives who delivered results in the field and in management. Kim Ki-hwan of GS Energy has led its renewable energy and new business strategy, and Kim Young-ju of GS Caltex pushed for more efficient operations and digital transformation at its production sites. Kang Yoon-seok of GS Retail helped improve the company's earnings structure, and Sung Nag-hyun of GS E&C has three decades of procurement experience. All four were promoted to senior executive vice president. GS kept the CEOs of its major affiliates but nominated new chief executives for four energy and power generation subsidiaries. Kim Jin-hak was tapped for Incheon Total Energy Company, Lee Jong-jin for GS Gumi Combined Heat and Power Plant, Heo Chang-ik for GS Donghae Electric Power and Yeo Seung-sub for GS Banwol Combined Heat and Power Plant. The appointments are seen as a response to changes in the electricity market and an effort to keep the subsidiaries' power plants running reliably. The group also stepped up efforts to develop its next generation of leaders. GS named 24 new vice presidents, a 33.3 percent increase from 18 in each of the previous two reshuffles. Eight are in their 40s. GS E&C named 10 new executives, double the number in its previous reshuffle. The appointments span its core housing and urban redevelopment businesses as well as future growth areas such as property development and data centers. GS EPS put a new vice president in their 40s in charge of the future business division at its power policy headquarters. "With uncertainty high at home and abroad, we chose stability so that our major affiliates can carry on with the business innovation they have been pursuing," a GS official said. "We will continue to support each affiliate in strengthening the profitability and competitiveness of its core business and in finding new growth engines through cooperation among affiliates, so that they can deliver tangible results." Under the theme of “discovering and growing founders,” Comeup 2026 will kick off on Dec. 9, with the number of corporate participants in its open innovation program reaching 65 this year. Chinese battery makers including CATL are partnering with Korean materials suppliers and Western automakers to expand abroad as U.S. and European Union rules seek to reduce reliance on China-made EV batteries. The company will retire 2.65 percent of its shares on Dec. 2 in a 1.73 trillion won move aimed at boosting shareholder value. The retailer in corporate rehabilitation cites a cash shortage and supply disruptions, while a potential sale remains under review.

title: GS Promotes Fourth-Generation Heir Hur Seo-hong to President - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
GS Group Executive Reshuffle
40 Executives Promoted, Including President Lee Tae-hyung
Hur Joo-hong and Hur Chi-hong Named Executive Vice Presidents
Priority on Earnings Growth Amid Stability GS Group (078930) promoted Hur Seo-hong, chief executive of GS Retail (007070) and a fourth-generation member of the founding family, to president. Heads of the group's main affiliates kept their posts given the uncertain business environment, with changes limited to the leaders of four energy and power subsidiaries, underscoring a focus on earnings growth within stability. GS announced its regular executive appointments for 2027 on the 25th, covering 40 people in total: two promotions to president, four appointments as chief executive, six promotions to executive vice president, four to senior vice president and 24 new vice presidents. Lee Tae-hyung, executive vice president of GS Holdings, was also elevated to president, while Hur Joo-hong, a senior vice president at GS Caltex, and Hur Chi-hong, head of GS Retail's strategy division — both fourth-generation family members — take the title of executive vice president. Born in 1977, Hur Seo-hong is the eldest son of Samyang International Chairman Hur Kwang-soo and a cousin once removed of GS Group Chairman Hur Tae-soo. Hur began a career as an analyst at Samjong KPMG before moving through GS Home Shopping, GS ITM and GS Energy, becoming chief executive of GS Retail in 2025. In the third quarter of this year, GS Retail posted record quarterly revenue and operating profit as margins improved at its convenience store, supermarket and home shopping businesses. Hur plans to sustain that growth by strengthening the customer-focused core business and accelerating management innovation built on an artificial intelligence transformation. Lee, born in 1970, joined Honam Oil Refinery — now GS Caltex — as an engineer at its Yeosu plant in 1994, later working at GS Energy and GS Power before serving as senior vice president and chief executive of Incheon Total Energy in 2019. Lee was promoted to executive vice president of GS Holdings in 2023, having built expertise in finance and mergers and acquisitions, including leading the acquisition of Incheon Total Energy. Lee will review investment priorities and funding plans for new businesses pursued jointly by affiliates and support Chairman Hur Tae-soo's future growth strategy. Hur Joo-hong, a son of GS E&C standing adviser Hur Myung-soo, will head the C&L division overseeing the petrochemical and lubricant businesses. Hur Chi-hong, a son of GS Caltex adviser Hur Jin-soo, will seek growth opportunities in overseas business and investment, drawing on experience in convenience store sales and merchandising as well as coordinating group-wide strategy. "With considerable uncertainty at home and abroad, we chose to maintain stability and let the main affiliates carry on the business innovation they have been pursuing," a GS official said. "We will continue to support each affiliate in strengthening profitability and competitiveness in its core areas and in finding new growth engines through cooperation among affiliates to deliver tangible results." title: GS Retail CEO Promoted to President After Record Quarter - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
Promotion comes about two years after he took the helm in early 2025
Focus on "fundamentals" drove six straight quarters of profit growth Huh Seo-hong, chief executive of GS Retail (007070), has been promoted to president two years after taking the top job, a move seen as recognition within the group for driving growth at the convenience store chain GS25, the supermarket chain GS The Fresh and the home shopping network GS Shop, including six consecutive quarters of year-on-year operating profit gains. GS Retail said on the 25th that Huh was promoted from executive vice president to president in GS Group's regular executive reshuffle for 2027, announced the same day. The promotion comes two years after he became chief executive of GS Retail in 2025. Since Huh took office, GS Retail has posted year-on-year increases in operating profit for six straight quarters, from the second quarter of last year through the third quarter of this year. In the third quarter, the company posted revenue of 3.31 trillion won ($2.3 billion) and operating profit of 132.1 billion won ($91 million), its best quarterly results on record. Since becoming chief executive, Huh has emphasized management focused on fundamentals, including strengthening the core business and pursuing profitable growth. One example is his push for a so-called scrap-and-build strategy at GS25, aimed at lifting sales at existing stores rather than expanding the store count. Existing stores were relocated to better nearby locations, and the company added more stores with expanded fresh food sections to target demand for grocery shopping close to home. The number of such stores roughly doubled to 1,074 in September this year from 557 at the end of 2024. These stores, which carry a wider range of fresh produce, fruit and meat, generate about 1 million won more in daily sales than regular outlets. GS25 posted record revenue of 2.47 trillion won ($1.7 billion) in the third quarter. GS The Fresh, the supermarket chain, expanded mainly through franchising and raised the share of quick commerce to 10.1%. Third-quarter revenue reached 527.7 billion won ($364 million), topping 500 billion won for the first time in a quarter. The number of stores rose to 608 at the end of September this year from 531 at the end of 2024. GS Shop, the home shopping unit, has logged four consecutive quarters of year-on-year improvement by expanding differentiated products, including building Core Authentic into a fashion brand with annual orders of 100 billion won ($69 million). In a corporate value enhancement plan for 2026 announced in August, GS Retail set a medium- to long-term target of 380 billion won ($262 million) in operating profit by 2028. "We plan to focus first on strengthening the core competitiveness of our convenience store, supermarket and home shopping businesses through management centered on fundamentals," a GS Retail official said. "We will gradually flesh out our blueprint for new businesses and expanded overseas operations to achieve sustainable growth." Huh is a fourth-generation member of the family that controls GS Group. He began his career in 2002 as an analyst in the corporate finance division of Samjong KPMG. He joined the new business team at GS Home Shopping in 2005, worked at Chevron and GS Energy from 2009, and headed the future business team at GS Holdings in 2020. He served as head of the management strategy service unit at GS Retail in 2023 before becoming chief executive in 2025. Original reporting by Kim Heung-rok for Seoul Economic Daily. title: GS Group promotes retail CEO Hur Suh-hong, retains key affiliate heads - Chosunbiz
content: GS Group reshuffles 40 executives, prioritizing management continuity Hur Suh-hong, CEO of GS Retail and a fourth-generation member of GS Group's founding family, has been promoted to president. Two other family members, GS Caltex executive vice president Hur Joo-hong and GS Retail strategy chief Huh Chi-hong, were promoted to vice president. GS Group also retained the CEOs of its major affiliates and replaced the heads of only four energy and power generation subsidiaries in an executive reshuffle focused on stability. GS Group carried out its regular executive reshuffle for 2027 on the 25th, affecting a total of 40 people, including two promotions to president, four CEO appointments, six promotions to vice president, four promotions to executive vice president and 24 new appointments as senior vice president. The two promoted to president are Hur Suh-hong, CEO and vice president of GS Retail, and Lee Tae-hyung, a vice president at GS Corp. Both were born in the 1970s and are expected to bring younger leadership to the executive team and lead the group's growth and business innovation. Hur Suh-hong was born in 1977 and is the eldest son of Hur Kwang-soo, chairman of Samyang International. He is also the nephew of GS Group Chairman Huh Tae-soo. Hur previously oversaw business operations and management at GS Energy and led the acquisition of Hugel as head of the future business team at holding company GS Corp. He later headed GS Retail's management strategy unit, overseeing strategy, finance and new businesses, before becoming its CEO last year. As CEO of GS Retail, Hur has worked to strengthen the core capabilities of its main businesses while using artificial intelligence (AI) to transform the company. Building on those efforts, GS Retail posted its highest-ever quarterly consolidated revenue and operating profit in the third quarter of this year, helped by improved profitability at its convenience store, supermarket and home shopping businesses. Lee Tae-hyung, the other executive promoted to president, was born in 1970 and began his career as an engineer at the Yeosu plant of Honam Oil Refinery, now GS Caltex. Lee served as head of management planning at GS Energy and CEO of Incheon Total Energy. He was promoted to vice president in 2023 and managed the group's finances and business portfolio as chief financial officer (CFO) and Head of Team for portfolio management at GS Corp. Lee was recognized for maintaining the group's financial health while drawing on his operational and investment experience to help identify future growth drivers, including AI data centers. A GS Group spokesperson said, "Lee's promotion reinforces our efforts to develop new businesses on a stable financial foundation and expand the business portfolio to support the group's growth." Among the fourth generation of the founding family, Hur Joo-hong, head of GS Caltex's basic chemicals division, and Huh Chi-hong, head of strategy, were each promoted from executive vice president to vice president. Hur Joo-hong previously headed the crude oil team at the Singapore subsidiary and the production digital transformation division at the Yeosu plant, and most recently led the basic chemicals division. Hur will oversee the petrochemical and lubricant businesses as head of the Chemical & Lube (C&L) division, with plans to improve profitability and medium- to long-term competitiveness. Huh Chi-hong has worked in convenience store operations and product planning and has experience coordinating companywide strategy. Building on that experience, Huh will support the execution of key initiatives in each business and identify new growth opportunities in overseas operations and investments. ◇ CEOs of major affiliates retained; only heads of 4 energy and power subsidiaries replaced GS Group retained the CEOs of its major affiliates in its 2027 reshuffle. That contrasts with last year, when it substantially revamped its management by appointing new CEOs at nine affiliates, including GS Global, GS Entec, GS E&R and GS P&L. GS Group said, "With uncertainty in the business environment growing this year due to high interest rates, geopolitical risks and the restructuring of global supply chains, we decided to leave operations in the hands of existing executives who know each business well." The company added, "The executives entrusted with major responsibilities in last year's reshuffle plan to continue the innovation initiatives they have pursued while adjusting implementation plans to reflect policy changes at home and abroad and market trends." It said the aim was to continue improving the profitability and competitiveness of its core businesses. However, GS Group designated new CEOs for four energy and power generation subsidiaries to respond to changes in the electricity market and ensure stable operation of power facilities. It selected Kim Jin-hak, head of business strategy and overseas investment at GS Energy, for Incheon Total Energy, and Lee Jong-jin, head of procurement at GS E&R, for GS Gumi Combined Heat and Power. Hur Chang-ik, head of management administration, was designated the new CEO of GS Donghae Electric Power, while Yeo Seung-seop, head of power generation, was named CEO of GS Banwol Combined Heat and Power. GS also appointed 24 new senior vice presidents in the reshuffle. That was an increase from the 18 appointed in the 2025 and 2026 reshuffles. Eight of the 24 new senior vice presidents are in their 40s. A GS Group spokesperson said, "We retained the CEOs of our major affiliates to ensure management continuity while promoting younger talent with proven expertise. We will continue to support each affiliate as it strengthens profitability and competitiveness in its core businesses and works with other affiliates to identify new growth drivers and deliver tangible results." On the 25th, GS Group announced its regular executive appointments for fiscal year 2027, covering a total of 40 individuals: two promotions to president, four appointments as representative directors, six promotions to vice president, four promotions to senior executive vice president, and 24 new appointments as executive vice presidents. As Head of the Future Business Team at GS Corp., he led the acquisition of Hugel, contributing to the diversification of the group's businesses. He subsequently served as Head of the Management Strategy Service Unit (SU) at GS Retail before taking office as Representative Director last year. President Heo has driven structural improvements at GS Retail by strengthening core competencies in key businesses and promoting innovation in work processes and organizational culture based on AX (AI transformation). In the third quarter of this year, GS Retail recorded its highest-ever quarterly consolidated revenue and operating profit, driven by improved profitability in its convenience store, supermarket, and home shopping segments. Born in 1970, President Lee joined Honam Refining & Petrochemicals (now GS Caltex) as an engineer at the Yeosu plant in 1994. He has served in various roles, including Head of the Management Planning Division at GS Energy and Representative Director of Incheon Comprehensive Energy. He possesses extensive experience ranging from power generation sites to strategy formulation, finance, and M&A (mergers and acquisitions). Since his promotion to vice president in 2023, he has managed the group's finances and business portfolio as CFO (Chief Financial Officer) and Head of the Portfolio Management (PM) Team at GS Corp. He was recognized for supporting the discovery of future growth drivers, such as AI data centers, while maintaining the group's financial soundness. Going forward, he is expected to review investment priorities and funding plans for new businesses jointly pursued by subsidiaries, thereby underpinning Chairman Hwang Tae-soo of GS Group's future growth strategy. Additionally, unlike last year when GS Group replaced the CEOs of nine subsidiaries, including GS Global, GS Entec, GS E&R, and GS P&L, this year it retained the CEOs of major subsidiaries. This move aims to continue the innovation initiatives pursued by existing management teams and enhance the profitability and competitiveness of core businesses, given increased uncertainty in the business environment due to high interest rates, geopolitical risks, and the restructuring of global supply chains. However, to respond to changes in the electricity market and ensure stable operation of power generation facilities, the company will replace the CEOs of four energy and power generation subsidiaries. Kim Jin-hak, Head of the Business Strategy and Overseas Investment Division at GS Energy, has been nominated as CEO of Incheon Comprehensive Energy. Lee Jong-jin, Head of the Procurement Division at GS E&R, has been nominated as CEO of GS Gumi Cogeneration Power Plant. Heo Chang-ik, Head of the Management Control Division, and Yeo Seung-seop, Head of the Power Generation Division, have been nominated as CEOs of GS Donghae Electric Power and GS Banwol Cogeneration Power Plant, respectively. Six individuals were promoted to vice president from four subsidiaries: GS Energy, GS Caltex, GS Retail, and GS Construction. At GS Energy, Kim Ki-hwan, Head of the Future Energy Division and Representative Director of GS Chargebee, who has led renewable energy business and new business strategy, was promoted to vice president. He is expected to identify domestic and international business opportunities in response to increased electricity demand driven by the spread of AI and strengthen the competitiveness of the electric vehicle charging business. At GS Caltex, Heo Ju-hong, Head of the Basic Chemicals Division, and Kim Young-ju, Head of the Value Chain and Profit Optimization (VCPO) Division, were promoted to vice president. Vice President Heo, born in 1983, will serve as Head of the Chemical & Lube (C&L) Headquarters, overseeing the petrochemical and lubricant businesses.
